AZ-2026-SB1683.aiSummary: The law limits foreign adversary nations and their agents from buying, leasing, or otherwise gaining a substantial interest in real property in Arizona. It also bars them from installing or operating certain equipment, like antennas, surveillance devices, or sensors, on property in the state. Beginning January 1, 2027, some utilities and government agencies must report suspected lease or equipment deals to the attorney general and the corporation commission. The law was signed by the governor and takes effect immediately.

AZ-2026-SB1627.aiSummary: This law changes Arizona rules on drones and model aircraft. It makes it illegal to fly them in ways that break federal rules, interfere with emergency work, or intentionally fly over or near certain critical sites for a crime. It also bars local governments from making their own drone rules in most cases, with some exceptions for public agencies, first responders, and a few city park rules.

AZ-2026-SB1452.title: cargo theft task force

documents.label: House COW 04/16 - Amended by TI - Biasiucci

AZ-2026-SB1452.aiSummary: Arizona would require the attorney general to set up a cargo theft task force to fight theft, fraud, and other crimes tied to cargo and freight. The task force would include law enforcement staff and would investigate cases, work with other agencies and industry partners, and suggest cases for prosecution. Starting July 1, 2027, the attorney general would send a yearly report on the task force's work and cargo theft trends.

AZ-2026-SB1270.aiSummary: The bill lets some correctional officers in the state retirement plan get an extra employer payment into their retirement account. The extra payment can be up to $5,000 per worker, can be given at set service milestones, and does not require the worker to add more money. It also says these payments are optional for employers and can be stopped later.

AZ-2026-SB1221.aiSummary: The bill would limit when the tax department can apply a new reading of tax law to taxpayers, and it would block retroactive tax, penalty, or interest charges in those cases. It would also require notice to the Senate Finance and House Ways & Means committees before a new reading is adopted, and it would allow a hearing on its effect on taxpayers. The measure would also set rules for refunds tied to past tax amounts and define "new interpretation or application" to include rules, tax rulings, procedures, and return instructions.

AZ-2026-SB1165.title: insurance; cost sharing; breast exams

documents.label: SENATE FACT SHEET: 02/18/2026 FIN As Passed Committee

AZ-2026-SB1165.aiSummary: The bill makes some health plans stop charging copays, deductibles, and other out-of-pocket costs for certain breast exams. It applies to hospital service corporations, health care service organizations, and disability insurers for policies or contracts issued, changed, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027. For high-deductible plans, the no-cost rule generally starts after the deductible is met, with an exception for preventive care.

AZ-2026-SB1046.title: telecommunications infrastructure; equipment requirements

documents.label: SENATE FACT SHEET: 06/24/2026 PS As Vetoed
SENATE FACT SHEET: 03/10/2026 PS As Passed Committee

AZ-2026-SB1046.aiSummary: The bill would bar Arizona telecommunications infrastructure from using equipment made by China or other foreign-adversary companies, and would require providers to remove and replace banned equipment. It would also require providers to certify each year to the Corporation Commission that they are not using banned equipment, and it sets civil penalties of at least $10,000 per day and up to $100,000 per day for violations. Providers that do not comply could also be blocked from receiving certain state, local, and federal money for telecommunications infrastructure. If enacted, it would take effect after December 31, 2026.

AZ-2026-HB2970.aiSummary: The bill would update Arizona’s fraud law to say the state can prosecute a case if one part of the scheme happened in Arizona or within one local area here, even if other parts happened elsewhere. It would also say that a fraud scheme includes taking away a person’s right to honest services. The change would affect people charged with fraudulent schemes and artifices.

SENATE FACT SHEET: 03/27/2026 HHS As Passed Committee

AZ-2026-HB2830.aiSummary: The bill would have required Arizona schools to teach fetal and prenatal human development in science classes, with the state board setting the grade levels and standards. It would have required lessons on stages of development, major milestones, and support structures like the placenta and umbilical cord. Schools would not have been allowed to include sex education topics in this instruction, and parents would not have had opt-out rights for it under the bill's rules. It was vetoed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2592.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for Arizona state agencies and other budget units on how they use artificial intelligence. It would require them to look for ways to use AI to cut admin work, lower costs, improve service, and use existing staff and resources, and it would limit new AI-specific rules unless the legislature clearly allows them. It would also require emergency or temporary AI rules to be ratified by the legislature. The bill was passed by both chambers but was later vetoed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2305.aiSummary: The bill would make private towing rates for cars from private property a state matter, so counties, cities, and towns could not add more local rules on those rates. In places that had not set rates by January 1, 2026, the towing, storage, and impound rate would follow the Department of Public Safety tow service agreement for that area, and local governments that already set rates would have to update them by July 1, 2027. It would also set rules for tow signs, photos, police notice, vehicle release, receipts, and penalties for private towing carriers and some property owners.
